meta.description: Akasha: existing agent runtime and isolated Windows consumer beta, with sourced documents and local OCR, confirmed reminders, recurring watches, scoped remote consent, SQLCipher memory and encrypted profile backups.

nodes.label: Tauri UI
nodes.description: Desktop React/TypeScript app (Chat, Tasks, Calendar, Memory, Router, Settings, and first-party module catalog). Talks to the daemon on port 3876.

nodes.label: TUI
nodes.description: Terminal interface with 7+ tabs (Chat, Scheduled returns, Router, Docs, Tasks, Calendar, Memory). Same slash commands as the UI.

nodes.label: CLI
nodes.description: Operator CLI: init, start/stop/up, doctor, vault, config, router, plugin, tui. Supervises the daemon process.

nodes.label: Slack
nodes.description: Slack adapter: signature verify, parse payload, build MessageEnvelope, poll and post replies.

nodes.label: Teams
nodes.description: Microsoft Teams / Bot Framework adapter with JWT validation and conversation-scoped envelopes.

nodes.label: Discord
nodes.description: Discord channel adapter; inbound messages normalize through the gateway / API path.

nodes.label: Telegram
nodes.description: Telegram bot adapter with cross-channel slash commands (/status, /budget, /permissions, /memory, /tasks).

nodes.label: Voice (TTS/STT)
nodes.description: Optional local voice path via speech_synthesize / speech_transcribe tools and voice_router.yaml.

nodes.label: Companion LAN
nodes.description: Companion software client discovered over UDP :3877; ESP32 firmware remains planned. Pairing is disabled unless AKASHA_COMPANION_PAIR_SECRET is set; data routes require a paired-device Bearer token.

nodes.label: HTTP API :3876
nodes.description: HTTP surface: health, message, tasks, memory, router, plugins, MCP, calendar, workspace graph, Companion LAN pairing, capabilities. CSRF on mutating routes. Routes split across api_routes_*; LLM tool loop in api_llm_loop. First-party module discovery and strict free-model controls are also exposed here.

nodes.label: Gateway
nodes.description: Normalizes every channel into MessageEnvelope and calls handle_envelope → Main Agent. Spec 48.

nodes.label: Main Agent
nodes.description: Single user-facing entry: ack <500ms, create task, complexity classification, route Direct vs Guided/Orchestrated.

nodes.label: Supervisor
nodes.description: Complexity classifier choosing Direct / Guided / Orchestrated execution modes.

nodes.label: Orchestrator
nodes.description: Decomposes requests, assigns specialists, aggregates results, satisfaction check, multi-state pipeline in Orchestrated mode.

nodes.label: Conversation Worker
nodes.description: Direct-mode worker: LLM chat loop with tool calls (TOOL: lines), memory recall, final reply. Implementation: run_message_via_llm in api_llm_loop + api_tool_dispatch.

nodes.label: Specialist Agents
nodes.description: Roster: analyst, architect, frontend/backend/db/integration, QA, documentalist, creative, system, code, research, security_audit, financial, etc.

nodes.label: Event Bus
nodes.description: In-process event fan-out (UserRequestReceived, TaskCreated, TodoListUpdated, progress). Feeds UI SSE/polling.

nodes.label: Task Store
nodes.description: SQLite tasks, todos, pipeline context, schedules. Source of truth for task lifecycle.

nodes.label: Scheduler / Calendar
nodes.description: Cron schedules, wakeups, exceptions, calendar OAuth/CalDAV; fires tasks back into Main Agent.

nodes.label: Memory Orchestrator
nodes.description: recall_context: fuses short-term, vector, graph facts, episodic events, and policy preferences into one prompt block.

nodes.label: Short-term Memory
nodes.description: Session turns with compaction when context exceeds token budget; injected as recent conversation context.

nodes.label: Vector Memory
nodes.description: memory_entries with ONNX/fastembed embeddings; hybrid keyword + semantic search.

nodes.label: Graph / Facts
nodes.description: Structured subject–predicate–object facts linked to memory entries for relational recall.

nodes.label: Episodic Memory
nodes.description: Significant events journal (preferences, promotions, task outcomes) with importance/scope metadata.

nodes.label: LLM Router
nodes.description: Task-type classifier, route config, provider manager, fallback engine, streaming, metrics. Config: llm_router.yaml. Optional strict free mode blocks paid-provider fallback.

nodes.label: Cloud Providers
nodes.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Azure, Google — selected per task_type primary/fallback.

nodes.label: Local Providers
nodes.description: Ollama and custom local OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

nodes.label: Embedded LLM
nodes.description: Bundled Candle (Qwen3 0.6B) or llama.cpp GGUF (CUDA default Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_K_M). Evidence via GET /api/capabilities + embedded-status; Rbitnet/DLM no-go v0.11.

nodes.label: Tools Engine
nodes.description: File/shell/web/browser/memory/device/voice tools; agentic TOOL: loop with policy filtering.

nodes.label: Tools Policy
nodes.description: tools_policy.yaml: allowed paths, commands, web domains, device interfaces, timeouts.

nodes.label: Vault
nodes.description: OS keyring + encrypted file secrets. Agents never see secrets unless VAULT: substitution is authorized.

nodes.label: Policy Engine
nodes.description: Permissions center / ask_me vs allow_all, constitution, budget checks around tool and channel actions.

nodes.label: Plugin Host (WASM)
nodes.description: Wasmtime sandbox for channel/tool/skill plugins declared via akasha-plugin-api manifests.

nodes.label: Plugin API
nodes.description: Manifest and capability contracts for plugins (channel, tool, skill, MCP).

nodes.label: MCP Runtime
nodes.description: MCP runtime stdio: probe, policy mcp_servers / tools_policy, CLI/UI operator (Implemented v0.11). OAuth vault = stretch.

nodes.label: RAG / Spec
nodes.description: Retrieval over product specs and runbooks for doctor --advice, system agent, and grounded answers.

nodes.label: Workspace Graph
nodes.description: Project knowledge graph: index, search, and expose codebase/workspace structure to agents.

nodes.label: akasha-core
nodes.description: Shared types, EventEnvelope, Spec Loader, prompt security helpers. No store/LLM/daemon deps.

nodes.label: Cluster (optional)
nodes.description: NATS, leader election, mTLS for multi-node deployments. Optional; single-node is the default.

nodes.label: Evals
nodes.description: Security, runbook, and hallucination evaluation suite for release quality gates.

nodes.label: SQLite
nodes.description: Bundled rusqlite persistence for tasks, memory, facts, episodic events, schedules, metrics.

nodes.label: Code Studio
nodes.description: Web client for project-scoped coding work: model selection, conversation, Kanban, editor, preview, and task recovery. Uses the Akasha daemon on port 3876.

nodes.label: Studio Projects & Kanban
nodes.description: Project-scoped metadata, ticket relationships, prerequisites, acceptance evidence, and task links persisted by the daemon.

nodes.label: First-party Module Catalog
nodes.description: Read-only catalog for Akasha application modules; reports Code Studio requirements, install and runtime state, and launches the supported module.

nodes.label: Free Model Catalog
nodes.description: Refreshes OpenRouter and Hugging Face model metadata, filters compatible zero-price routes, and fails closed rather than calling paid providers when strict free mode is enabled.

nodes.label: Windows consumer beta
nodes.description: Separate portable desktop edition on port 3877, dedicated profile, three onboarding steps and restricted native transport.

nodes.label: Documents and local OCR
nodes.description: PDFium and Tesseract 5 in a cancellable worker; source/page/extraction references, model answers, source verification and Markdown export.

nodes.label: Scoped remote consent
nodes.description: Every remote model/search request requires an explicit recipient and data scope; child tasks inherit root scope and recurrent watches use revocable grants.

nodes.label: SQLCipher memory
nodes.description: Consumer beta encrypts the whole long-term memory database. Windows Credential Manager protects a random key; missing keys lock memory instead of creating an empty replacement.

nodes.label: Notes to confirmed reminders
nodes.description: Model proposals have no scheduling effects; explicit confirmation resolves ambiguous local dates and persists actions/reminders idempotently.

nodes.label: Personal recurring watch
nodes.description: Existing scheduler and search engine produce dated reports with novelty, seen items and unavailable sources; missed periods resume at most once.

nodes.label: Encrypted profile backup
nodes.description: Argon2id and AES-256-GCM archive; restore validates in a separate directory and activation waits for restart; remote grants and service credentials are excluded.

nodes.label: Usage qualification evidence
nodes.description: Synthetic asynchronous probes and version-bound evidence for conversation, documents and actions; catalogue availability alone never recommends a model.

flows.name: Direct chat (UI → reply)
flows.description: User sends a simple message from Tauri/TUI. Gateway creates an envelope; Main Agent acks, Supervisor chooses Direct, Conversation worker recalls memory, calls LLM Router, optionally runs tools, then returns the answer.

flows.name: Guided / Orchestrated multi-agent
flows.description: Complex request: Supervisor routes to Orchestrator, which decomposes via LLM, delegates to specialists with tools, aggregates, satisfaction-checks, then delivers.

flows.name: Slack inbound message
flows.description: Slack adapter verifies signature, builds MessageEnvelope, handle_envelope → Main Agent; reply polled and posted back to Slack.

flows.name: Telegram via API path
flows.description: Telegram client posts to /api/message; same normalized gateway path as the UI.

flows.name: 4-layer memory recall
flows.description: Before generation, Memory Orchestrator fuses short-term, vector hits, graph facts, and episodic events into the prompt context.

flows.name: Memory promote after task
flows.description: After a successful turn, promote extracts document + facts + episodic event into SQLite-backed layers.

flows.name: Tool call with vault secret
flows.description: Agent emits TOOL: run_command; policy authorizes; vault substitutes secrets; result returns to the LLM loop.

flows.name: LLM primary → fallback chain
flows.description: Router classifies task_type, tries primary provider, then fallbacks through cloud/local/embedded per llm_router.yaml.

flows.name: Scheduled / calendar wakeup
flows.description: Scheduler fires a cron or calendar wakeup, creates a task through Main Agent, and delivers the result to scheduled-returns UI.

flows.name: WASM plugin tool
flows.description: Agent selects a tool plugin; Plugin Host runs it in Wasmtime sandbox under declared permissions.

flows.name: MCP external tool
flows.description: MCP runtime lists/calls tools on an attached stdio or SSE server; results feed back into the agent loop.

flows.name: Doctor with RAG advice
flows.description: CLI doctor --advice retrieves runbooks via RAG and asks the LLM for grounded remediation tips (daemon required).

flows.name: Workspace knowledge graph
flows.description: Conversation or specialist queries the workspace graph for project structure and symbols while coding.

flows.name: Browser automation tool
flows.description: Agent uses browser navigate/snapshot (Playwright per task) under allowed_web_domains policy.

flows.name: Voice in / voice out
flows.description: Microphone capture → speech_transcribe → chat path; reply → speech_synthesize → audio playback.
UI or doctor queries GET /api/capabilities and embedded-status before marking GGUF/vision ready.
flows.name: Capabilities / evidence
Companion LAN discovery and pairing
flows.description: The client discovers the daemon over UDP :3877. Pairing checks a dedicated secret and returns a device token; subsequent Companion data routes require that paired Bearer token.

flows.name: Code Studio project planning and execution
flows.description: Code Studio registers a project and its Kanban backlog with the daemon, submits a task, and follows the ticket scheduler, scoped tools, verification outcomes, and recovery through the same project workspace.

flows.name: Discover and launch an Akasha module
flows.description: The Tauri client lists first-party modules and their requirements through the daemon catalog, then launches the supported Code Studio module.

flows.name: Strict free-model routing
flows.description: The router refreshes provider metadata, keeps only compatible zero-price candidates, and refuses paid-provider fallback while free mode is enabled.

flows.name: Understand my documents
flows.description: Local page extraction and OCR produce references; the ordinary task lifecycle routes an authorized answer and an export back to the desktop.

flows.name: Turn notes into reminders
flows.description: The model proposes actions, the user confirms concrete dates, then persisted reminders become visible.

flows.name: Recurring personal watch
flows.description: A separately authorized recurrence uses the existing scheduler and search tools to retain dated reports and avoid duplicate catch-up.

flows.name: Restore an encrypted profile
flows.description: A phrase-protected archive is checked in isolation before activation; the current data remains available until restart.
